title: App never sends `noCoupon`, so removing a coupon silently re-applies one server-side (charge ≠ displayed total, one-time spin reward burnt)
detail: placeOrder on the server treats `couponCode: null` as "auto-apply the best offer" and only treats it as "no coupon" when `noCoupon: true` (or `couponCode: ''`) is sent — functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:530-538. The web client sends it (`noCoupon: !draft.coupon`, web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:364). The Flutter repository's placeOrder payload (checkout_repository.dart:421-430) has no `noCoupon` field at all, and both app call sites pass `couponCode: draft.coupon?.code` which is null once the coupon is cleared (checkout_screen.dart:219, payment_screen.dart:149). The app DOES offer a clear action: the applied-coupon chip's × calls `setCoupon(null)` (widgets/coupon_apply.dart:199), and `_resyncApplied` also auto-clears a coupon that falls below its minimum (coupon_apply.dart:143-152).
failure_scenario: Customer has a ₹200 spin coupon they want to save for a bigger order. On the app Checkout screen it is auto-applied, they tap × to remove it, the summary re-renders at 'To pay ₹1,000' and they place a COD order. placeOrder receives couponCode=null, noCoupon absent → autoBestOffer() picks the same spin coupon, discounts ₹200, marks customers/{uid}/coupons/{id} status 'used', and writes an order with totalPaise 800. The rider collects ₹800 for an order the customer was shown as ₹1,000, and the one-time reward is spent without consent. Same happens when _resyncApplied auto-clears a coupon.
fix: Add `'noCoupon': draft.coupon == null` (or an explicit bool param) to the placeOrder payload in CheckoutRepository.placeOrder and pass it from both checkout_screen._placeOrder and payment_screen._pay, mirroring web callPlaceOrder.

title: App auto-applies promo coupons without checking per-user usage limits; admin stamps `maxUsesPerUser: 1` on every coupon, so a returning customer's checkout is hard-rejected
detail: app listAvailableOffers() filters promos only on status/targetUsers/autoApply/expiry/minimum (offers.dart:99-125). It never checks `maxUsesPerUser`, `usesCount` vs `maxUsesTotal`, or `validFrom`. checkout_screen._autoApplyBestOffer (checkout_screen.dart:334-353) takes the first qualifying entry and writes it straight into the draft, and it is then sent as an EXPLICIT couponCode, which the server validates in full: functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:243-250 throws 'This coupon has reached its usage limit.' / 'You have already used this coupon.' and :233-236 throws for validFrom. admin/src/features/coupons/api/coupons.ts:158 writes `maxUsesPerUser: 1` on EVERY newly created coupon, so this fires for essentially every promo. The web deliberately excludes these from auto-apply (web/src/components/checkout/offers.ts:117-124), exactly matching the server's autoBestOffer (checkout.ts:354-362).
failure_scenario: Admin creates promo SAVE10 (active, targetUsers 'all', ₹100 off) → doc carries maxUsesPerUser: 1. Customer opens the app Checkout: SAVE10 is auto-applied and the order goes through (first use). On their NEXT order the app auto-applies SAVE10 again; placeOrder throws failed-precondition 'You have already used this coupon.' and the customer cannot place ANY order until they discover the × on the coupon chip. Secondary money impact: because the app auto-applies coupons the store limited to manual entry, every first app order silently receives the best promo discount that a web order never gets.
fix: Port web evalPromo's rejections into app offers.dart: skip promos with `maxUsesPerUser > 0`, with `firstOrderOnly == true`, with `usesCount >= maxUsesTotal`, and with `validFrom > now` — for the auto-apply/banner path at minimum.

title: App ignores a coupon's `applicableCategories`, so the app shows a larger discount than the server grants and the customer is charged more than the screen (and Razorpay sheet) said
detail: app `_discount()` (offers.dart:53-69) computes flat/percent discounts against the WHOLE cart subtotal; nothing in the app ever reads `applicableCategories`. The server restricts both validity and amount to the eligible lines: discountableSubtotal() (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:162-168) and computeCouponDiscount() (checkout.ts:265-283) clamp the discount to the category subtotal, or reject the coupon outright when it is 0. The web mirrors the server (web/src/components/checkout/offers.ts:72-83, and it passes each line's categorySlug in). The client value is what the app renders in `_summaryCard` and in the pay-bar label, and — because coupon_screen.dart:69-71 and _autoApplyBestOffer set the draft from the CLIENT number without calling applyCoupon — it is never corrected before placement.
failure_scenario: Coupon SPICE20 = 20% off, applicableCategories ['spices']. Cart = ₹2,000 total of which ₹500 is spices. App shows Discount −₹400, 'To pay ₹1,600'. COD: placeOrder computes eligible ₹500 → discount ₹100 → order totalPaise ₹1,900; the rider collects ₹1,900. Razorpay: the pay bar says 'Pay ₹1,600' but createRazorpayOrder returns 1,90,000 paise and payment_screen.dart:218 opens the sheet with `rzp.amountPaise`, so the customer is charged ₹1,900 after being quoted ₹1,600.
fix: Pass the cart lines (productId → categorySlug + lineTotal) into app listAvailableOffers and implement discountableSubtotal exactly as web offers.ts:72-83 does; drop coupons whose eligible subtotal is 0. Safest additional step: have the app confirm any client-selected coupon through the `applyCoupon` callable before showing a total (as coupon_screen.dart:46 already does for typed codes).

title: App places a SECOND order for the same cart if the customer leaves the Payment screen after a failed/cancelled payment — the placement nonce dies with the screen
detail: `_nonce` is `late final` on _PaymentScreenState (payment_screen.dart:46-47), i.e. per route instance. Checkout pushes a NEW PaymentScreen every time the pay bar is tapped (checkout_screen.dart:1073-1076, 1104-1105). After a gateway cancel/decline, _onPaymentError only sets `_processing = false` (payment_screen.dart:303-334) and the cart/draft are deliberately left intact; the customer can dismiss the screen with the header × (payment_screen.dart:521-527). On re-entry, `_pay()` calls placeOrder with a brand-new nonce, so the server's idempotency check (checkout.ts:605-625) does not match and a second order is created: stock decremented again (CheckoutHold was already cleared at line 163, so the full validate-and-decrement path runs), wallet debited again, a second `payments/{orderId}` row, a second shortId. Web keeps its nonce alive across a failed payment for exactly this reason (web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:346, 448-451).
failure_scenario: Wallet ₹200, cart ₹1,000, method razorpay. Tap Pay → order #BRK-1 placed, wallet −₹200, Razorpay opens for ₹800 → customer cancels → toast 'Payment cancelled'. They tap × to go back, then tap Pay again → order #BRK-2 placed, stock decremented a second time, wallet now 0 so Razorpay opens for the full ₹1,000, which they pay. Result: two orders, two stock decrements, and ₹200 of wallet money stranded in the unpaid #BRK-1 until it is manually cancelled.
fix: Hoist the placement nonce out of PaymentScreen State — e.g. into the CheckoutDraft / a `CheckoutAttempt` holder alongside CheckoutHold — generated once per checkout attempt and cleared only when an order completes or the draft resets.

title: Stock leaks permanently when the reservation holds more than the ordered lines: placeOrder consumes the whole hold without returning the surplus
detail: placeOrder honours a reservation when every ordered line is COVERED by it — `useReservation = [...wanted].every(([k, qty]) => (held.get(k) ?? 0) >= qty)` (checkout.ts:676-682). It then skips the stock decrement entirely (checkout.ts:777-787) and marks the reservation `status: 'consumed'` (checkout.ts:966-968). Units held but not ordered (a reduced qty, or a line that left the cart) are never given back: stockReservationSweep only restores reservations still `status == 'active'` (scheduled/sweeps.ts:130-135), and releaseStock is a no-op for a non-active reservation (reservations.ts:256). The web reserves exactly once per checkout mount and never re-reserves — `reserveStartedRef` guards the effect (web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:122-123) — while `lines` is live-bridged from `customers/{uid}.cart` and updates in place whenever the cart changes on any other surface (web/src/lib/cart.ts:262-281). The app re-reserves on a cart-signature change but skips it while another reserve is in flight without re-arming (checkout_screen.dart:142-149).
failure_scenario: Customer opens web /checkout with 2 × Cardamom (reserveStock takes products/cardamom.stock 10 → 8). On their phone they set the bag to 1 × Cardamom; the web page's cart updates live, but the reservation is not retaken. They click Place order: placeOrder sees wanted 1 ≤ held 2, skips the decrement, marks the reservation consumed. Stock stays at 8 although only 1 unit was sold — 1 unit is unsellable forever, with no sweep or manual release path short of an admin stock edit.
fix: In placeOrder's reservation branch, compute `surplus = held − wanted` per line key and restore it with restoreReservedStock() in the same transaction before marking the reservation consumed (the product snapshots are already in the read set); alternatively require an exact line/qty match to honour the hold and fall through to the decrement path otherwise.

title: App has no `waiveDelivery` support, so a free-shipping coupon shows delivery charged while the server waives it
detail: Server summarise() waives delivery for a `free_shipping` coupon: `const freeDelivery = waiveDelivery || subtotalPaise <= 0 || (threshold > 0 && net >= threshold)` (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:427), and applyCoupon returns the flag precisely so clients can mirror it (checkout.ts:454-458). Web does mirror it (web/src/components/checkout/checkout.ts:110-112). The app's AppliedCoupon has no such field (checkout_repository.dart:68-74), applyCoupon() drops it from the callable response (checkout_repository.dart:300-310), and computeSummary omits the term entirely (checkout_repository.dart:254-255). free_shipping coupons are a real, shippable prize type (admin CouponFormPage.tsx:30; app user_coupon.dart:79 renders 'Free delivery').
failure_scenario: Store charges ₹49 standard delivery. Customer wins a FREESHIP spin coupon and applies it on the app. Discount is ₹0 (correct) but the summary still shows Delivery ₹49 and 'To pay ₹549'. placeOrder waives delivery, writing deliveryPaise 0 / totalPaise 500. COD collects ₹500 against a screen that said ₹549; for razorpay the Pay button says ₹549 while the gateway sheet opens at ₹500.
fix: Add `waiveDelivery` to AppliedCoupon, read it from the applyCoupon response and from the offers list (`discountType == 'free_shipping'`), and OR it into the freeDelivery term in CheckoutRepository.computeSummary.

title: No way to pay an order whose online payment failed — both clients promise 'payable from My orders', but no retry-payment path exists
detail: markPaymentFailed is explicitly designed around a retry: 'the order still exists, its stock is still held, and the customer can retry payment from My Orders' (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:1095-1097). Both clients tell the customer exactly that (app payment_screen.dart:276, 332; web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:387, 420, 438). But `createRazorpayOrder` / `verifyPayment` have no caller anywhere outside the checkout/payment flow — grep over web/src and app/lib returns only components/checkout/checkout.ts and features/checkout/*. The customer order detail screens only render the payment status as text (web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/page.tsx:211-216). Meanwhile placeOrder has already debited the wallet, burnt the coupon and consumed the stock for that order (checkout.ts:822-839, 1016-1021, 960-968), and nothing ever expires an unpaid 'accepted' order.
failure_scenario: Customer places a ₹1,000 razorpay order using ₹200 of wallet, the card is declined, they dismiss the sheet. Order stays status 'accepted' / paymentStatus 'failed'. There is no 'Pay now' anywhere: their ₹200 wallet balance, their spin coupon and the reserved stock are all locked in an order they cannot pay. Their only exit is Cancel order (which refunds the wallet and restores stock) and starting over.
fix: Either surface a 'Complete payment' action on the customer order detail screen for `paymentStatus in ('pending','failed') && paymentMethod == 'razorpay' && status not cancelled` (createRazorpayOrder already reuses the existing gateway order, checkout.ts:1197-1199), or auto-cancel unpaid razorpay orders after a timeout in a scheduled sweep — and change the client copy to match whichever is chosen.

title: Cancellation/refund does not invalidate the published invoice
detail: performCancellation flips status/paymentStatus and refunds, but never clears `invoiceUrl` / `invoiceGeneratedAt` nor removes the Storage object (cancel.ts:226-234). generateInvoiceForOrder publishes `invoices/{shortId}.html` with a permanent `firebaseStorageDownloadTokens` token and stamps the URL on the order (invoice.ts:84-94). COD and fully-wallet-paid orders get an invoice at placement (checkout.ts:1077-1080), so a cancelled COD order keeps a downloadable document headed 'Tax Invoice' billing the full total. The admin UI already works around it manually by regenerating instead of reopening when `invoiceGeneratedAt < cancelledAt` (admin/src/features/orders/routes/OrderDetailPage.tsx:131-141), but the customer-facing 'Download PDF' link keeps pointing at the stale token URL (web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/invoice/page.tsx:108-109; app invoice_screen.dart:55-58 even shares the raw URL).
failure_scenario: Customer places a ₹5,000 COD order → invoice published and linked. They cancel it an hour later. Their Orders → Invoice screen still offers 'Download PDF', and the shared link still renders a full ₹5,000 Tax Invoice with no cancellation or credit-note marking, until an admin happens to press Generate invoice on that order.
fix: In performCancellation, clear `invoiceUrl`/`invoiceGeneratedAt` on the order (and optionally delete the Storage object), or call generateInvoiceForOrder after the transaction so the published document reflects the cancelled/refunded state.
